Plant: Apple
Watering: Water deeply when the soil begins to dry, especially during establishment and hot weather.
Sunlight: Full sun is preferred for good growth and fruiting.
Soil: Well-drained soil with organic matter.
Common problems: Apple scab and black rot.
Care: Remove fallen infected leaves and fruit, prune for airflow, and avoid unnecessary leaf wetness.

﻿Plant: Apple
Disease: Black Rot
Symptoms:
Dark, enlarging lesions can occur on leaves, fruit, and branches. Fruit may develop dark rot and eventually shrivel.
Management:
Remove infected fruit and plant material. Prune affected areas where appropriate and maintain good airflow.
Prevention:
Keep the growing area clean, remove fallen or diseased material, and avoid unnecessary leaf wetness.
Plant Care:
Provide full sun and well-drained soil. Maintain appropriate watering and avoid waterlogging.

﻿Plant: Apple
Disease: Rust
Symptoms:
Rust diseases can cause yellow, orange, or reddish lesions on leaves and may reduce plant vigor when infection is severe.
Management:
Remove heavily affected plant material where practical and improve airflow around the plant.
Prevention:
Maintain sanitation, good airflow, and avoid prolonged leaf wetness.
Plant Care:
Grow in full sun with well-drained soil and provide adequate moisture without waterlogging.

﻿Plant: Apple
Disease: Apple Scab
Symptoms:
Olive-green to brown spots can develop on leaves and fruit. Severe infection may cause leaf drop and affected fruit.
Management:
Remove and dispose of fallen infected leaves and affected fruit. Improve airflow by appropriate pruning. Avoid unnecessary leaf wetness.
Prevention:
Maintain good orchard sanitation, improve airflow, and avoid prolonged moisture on foliage.
Plant Care:
Provide full sun and well-drained soil. Water the root zone rather than repeatedly wetting the leaves.

﻿Plant: Cherry
Disease: Powdery Mildew
Symptoms:
A white, powdery fungal growth may appear on leaves and young shoots. Infected growth can become distorted or weakened.
Management:
Remove severely affected plant material where practical and improve airflow around the plant. Avoid excessive humidity around foliage.
Prevention:
Maintain good spacing and airflow, monitor new growth regularly, and avoid unnecessary prolonged leaf wetness.
Plant Care:
Provide appropriate sunlight, well-drained soil, and balanced moisture.

﻿Plant: Corn
Disease: Common Rust
Symptoms:
Small reddish-brown to rust-colored pustules may appear on corn leaves. Severe infection can reduce healthy leaf area.
Management:
Monitor plants regularly and manage the disease according to local agricultural recommendations. Remove severely affected material where practical.
Prevention:
Use healthy planting material, maintain appropriate plant spacing, and avoid conditions that keep foliage wet for long periods.
Plant Care:
Provide adequate sunlight, suitable soil moisture, and balanced nutrition.

﻿Plant: Corn
Disease: Gray Leaf Spot
Symptoms:
Gray to tan rectangular lesions can develop on corn leaves, often expanding along the leaf veins.
Management:
Monitor disease development and remove or manage infected crop residue according to local agricultural guidance.
Prevention:
Crop rotation and residue management can reduce disease pressure. Maintain suitable plant spacing and field airflow.
Plant Care:
Provide adequate moisture and balanced nutrition while avoiding unnecessary prolonged leaf wetness.

﻿Plant: Corn
Disease: Leaf Blight
Symptoms:
Leaf blight can produce brown or tan lesions on corn leaves. Severe infection can reduce photosynthetic leaf area.
Management:
Monitor affected plants and manage infected crop residue appropriately. Follow local agricultural recommendations for disease control.
Prevention:
Use healthy planting material, maintain crop rotation where appropriate, and reduce conditions that favor prolonged leaf wetness.
Plant Care:
Maintain adequate soil moisture and balanced nutrition.

﻿Plant: Corn
Disease: Northern Leaf Blight
Symptoms:
Long, elongated gray-green to tan lesions can develop on corn leaves and may expand significantly under favorable conditions.
Management:
Monitor plants regularly and manage infected crop residue according to local agricultural recommendations.
Prevention:
Crop rotation, residue management, and appropriate plant spacing can help reduce disease pressure.
Plant Care:
Maintain adequate soil moisture and balanced nutrition and avoid prolonged wetness on foliage where practical.

﻿Plant: Grape
Disease: Black Rot
Symptoms:
Small reddish-brown lesions may develop on leaves and berries. Infected berries can darken, shrivel, and develop black fruiting structures.
Management:
Remove infected berries and plant debris where practical. Improve canopy airflow and avoid unnecessary prolonged leaf wetness.
Prevention:
Maintain good vineyard sanitation, appropriate spacing, and airflow. Remove mummified fruit and infected debris.
Plant Care:
Provide adequate sunlight, well-drained soil, and appropriate irrigation without prolonged leaf wetness.

﻿Plant: Grape
Disease: Esca
Symptoms:
Esca is associated with wood-decay fungi and may cause leaf symptoms, reduced vine vigor, and decline of affected grapevines.
Management:
Remove severely affected or dead plant material where practical and maintain vineyard sanitation. Follow local agricultural guidance for management.
Prevention:
Use healthy planting material, make careful pruning cuts, and avoid unnecessary wounds to the vine.
Plant Care:
Provide adequate sunlight, appropriate irrigation, and good canopy airflow.

﻿Plant: Grape
Disease: Leaf Blight
Symptoms:
Leaf blight can produce discolored or necrotic areas on grape leaves and may reduce healthy leaf area when infection is severe.
Management:
Remove severely affected plant material where practical and improve canopy airflow. Avoid unnecessary prolonged leaf wetness.
Prevention:
Maintain vineyard sanitation, suitable plant spacing, and good airflow. Monitor leaves regularly.
Plant Care:
Provide adequate sunlight, well-drained soil, and appropriate irrigation.

﻿Plant: Orange
Disease: Citrus Greening
Symptoms:
Citrus greening can cause yellowing or mottled leaves, reduced tree vigor, and small or poorly colored fruit. Symptoms can vary across the tree.
Management:
Monitor trees regularly and follow local agricultural recommendations for management. Control of the insect vector and removal of severely affected trees may be recommended in affected production areas.
Prevention:
Use healthy, certified planting material where available and monitor for insect vectors. Follow regional citrus disease-management guidance.
Plant Care:
Provide adequate sunlight, appropriate irrigation, good drainage, and balanced nutrition.

﻿Plant: Peach
Disease: Bacterial Spot
Symptoms:
Small dark spots can develop on leaves and fruit. Severe leaf infection may cause shot-hole symptoms and premature leaf drop.
Management:
Remove severely affected plant material where practical and maintain good airflow. Follow local agricultural recommendations for bacterial disease management.
Prevention:
Use healthy planting material, maintain sanitation, and avoid unnecessary prolonged leaf wetness.
Plant Care:
Provide adequate sunlight, well-drained soil, and appropriate irrigation.

﻿Plant: Pepper Bell
Disease: Bacterial Spot
Symptoms:
Small water-soaked or dark lesions may develop on leaves, stems, and fruit. Severe infection can cause leaf loss and blemished fruit.
Management:
Remove severely affected plant material where practical. Avoid working with wet foliage and maintain good airflow.
Prevention:
Use healthy seed or planting material, maintain sanitation, avoid overhead irrigation when possible, and avoid unnecessary leaf wetness.
Plant Care:
Provide adequate sunlight, well-drained soil, and consistent moisture without waterlogging.

﻿Plant: Potato
Disease: Early Blight
Symptoms:
Dark brown lesions with concentric ring patterns may develop on older leaves. Severe infection can cause leaf yellowing and premature leaf loss.
Management:
Remove heavily infected foliage where practical and maintain good field sanitation. Avoid prolonged leaf wetness.
Prevention:
Practice crop rotation, use healthy planting material, maintain appropriate plant nutrition, and reduce prolonged moisture on foliage.
Plant Care:
Keep soil consistently moist during tuber development but avoid waterlogging. Provide full sun and well-drained soil.

﻿Plant: Potato
Disease: Late Blight
Symptoms:
Water-soaked or dark lesions may develop on leaves and stems. Under favorable conditions, lesions can expand rapidly and infected tissue may die.
Management:
Remove heavily infected foliage where practical and follow local agricultural recommendations for disease management. Avoid prolonged leaf wetness.
Prevention:
Use healthy planting material, maintain good field sanitation, improve airflow, and avoid unnecessary overhead irrigation.
Plant Care:
Keep soil adequately moist without waterlogging. Provide full sun and well-drained soil.

﻿Plant: Squash
Disease: Powdery Mildew
Symptoms:
White, powder-like fungal growth can appear on leaves and stems. Severely affected leaves may become yellow, dry, or weakened.
Management:
Remove severely affected leaves where practical and improve airflow around plants. Follow local agricultural recommendations for disease management.
Prevention:
Provide adequate plant spacing, good airflow, and avoid excessive conditions that favor disease development.
Plant Care:
Provide suitable sunlight, consistent soil moisture, and well-drained soil. Avoid unnecessary prolonged leaf wetness.

﻿Plant: Strawberry
Disease: Leaf Scorch
Symptoms:
Small dark purple, reddish, or brown spots can develop on strawberry leaves. Spots may enlarge and cause affected tissue to appear scorched.
Management:
Remove severely affected leaves where practical and maintain good airflow. Keep the growing area clean.
Prevention:
Avoid prolonged leaf wetness, maintain appropriate spacing, remove infected plant debris, and monitor plants regularly.
Plant Care:
Provide adequate sunlight, well-drained soil, and consistent moisture without waterlogging.

﻿Plant: Tomato
Disease: Bacterial Spot
Symptoms: Small dark water-soaked spots may appear on leaves, stems, and fruit. Spots can enlarge and become rough or scabby.
Management: Remove severely affected plant material and keep foliage as dry as practical. Improve airflow and avoid working with plants when leaves are wet.
Prevention: Use clean planting material, sanitize tools, provide adequate spacing, and avoid unnecessary overhead irrigation.
Plant Care: Monitor new growth regularly and maintain good drainage, sunlight, and airflow.

﻿Plant: Tomato
Disease: Early Blight
Symptoms: Dark brown lesions with concentric ring patterns commonly develop on older leaves. Severe infection can cause yellowing and leaf drop.
Management: Remove badly affected leaves, improve airflow, and avoid prolonged leaf wetness.
Prevention: Rotate crops where practical, remove infected plant debris, and keep foliage from contacting wet soil.
Plant Care: Water at the soil surface when possible and monitor lower leaves regularly.

﻿Plant: Tomato
Disease: Late Blight
Symptoms: Dark, irregular water-soaked lesions may develop on leaves and stems. Under humid conditions, affected areas can expand rapidly.
Management: Remove severely affected tissue and reduce prolonged leaf wetness. Separate heavily affected plants where practical.
Prevention: Maintain airflow, avoid unnecessary overhead watering, remove infected plant debris, and monitor plants during cool and humid weather.
Plant Care: Inspect leaves frequently and respond quickly when rapidly expanding dark lesions appear.

﻿Plant: Tomato
Disease: Leaf Mold
Symptoms: Pale yellow areas may develop on the upper leaf surface, with olive-green to brown mold-like growth commonly appearing on the underside.
Management: Improve ventilation and reduce humidity around foliage. Remove severely affected leaves and avoid prolonged leaf wetness.
Prevention: Provide adequate plant spacing, improve airflow, and water at the soil level when possible.
Plant Care: Keep foliage dry and inspect both sides of leaves in humid growing conditions.

﻿Plant: Tomato
Disease: Mosaic Virus
Symptoms: Leaves may show mottled light and dark green patterns, distortion, reduced growth, or irregular development.
Management: Remove strongly affected plants where appropriate and prevent mechanical spread through contaminated hands and tools.
Prevention: Use clean planting material, wash hands and tools, control potential insect vectors where relevant, and avoid handling healthy plants immediately after infected plants.
Plant Care: Monitor new leaves for mosaic patterns and unusual distortion.

﻿Plant: Tomato
Disease: Septoria Leaf Spot
Symptoms: Numerous small circular spots may develop on older leaves, often with pale centers and darker margins. Severe infection can cause leaf drop.
Management: Remove affected lower leaves and plant debris, improve airflow, and minimize leaf wetness.
Prevention: Provide adequate spacing, avoid overhead irrigation when possible, and remove infected debris after the growing season.
Plant Care: Inspect older leaves regularly and maintain good ventilation around plants.

﻿Plant: Tomato
Disease: Spider Mites
Symptoms: Fine webbing, stippled or speckled leaves, yellowing, and loss of leaf vigor may occur, especially during hot and dry conditions.
Management: Inspect leaf undersides and reduce plant stress. A strong but appropriate water spray can help dislodge mites on suitable plants.
Prevention: Avoid excessive plant stress and dusty conditions, and regularly inspect plants during hot, dry weather.
Plant Care: Maintain appropriate moisture and check the undersides of leaves for mites and webbing.

﻿Plant: Tomato
Disease: Target Spot
Symptoms: Brown circular lesions can develop on leaves and may show concentric target-like rings. Fruit may also develop dark lesions.
Management: Remove severely affected foliage, improve airflow, and reduce prolonged leaf wetness.
Prevention: Remove infected plant debris, provide adequate spacing, and avoid unnecessary overhead irrigation.
Plant Care: Monitor leaves and fruit regularly, especially under warm and humid conditions.

﻿Plant: Tomato
Disease: Yellow Leaf Curl Virus
Symptoms: Leaves may curl upward, become yellow, and show reduced growth. Plants can become stunted and fruit production may decline.
Management: Remove severely affected plants where appropriate and manage insect vectors such as whiteflies according to locally appropriate integrated pest management practices.
Prevention: Use healthy planting material, monitor for whiteflies, remove infected plants when practical, and control weeds that may support insect populations.
Plant Care: Inspect new growth frequently for curling, yellowing, and stunting.

General Plant Care
Yellow leaves can have multiple causes including overwatering, poor drainage, insufficient light, nutrient imbalance, natural aging, or disease.
Before watering, check the soil moisture rather than watering on a fixed schedule alone.
Good drainage and appropriate light are important for most houseplants.
Fertilizer should be selected according to the plant type and applied according to label directions.
If disease is suspected, isolate the affected plant where practical and avoid sharing unclean tools.

﻿Plant: Apple
Condition: Healthy
Care:
Provide full sun and well-drained soil with organic matter. Water deeply when the soil begins to dry, especially during hot or dry weather.
Prevention:
Maintain good airflow, remove fallen plant debris, monitor leaves and fruit regularly, and avoid unnecessary leaf wetness.
General Guidance:
Healthy plants should be monitored regularly for changes in leaves, stems, and fruit.

﻿Plant: Blueberry
Condition: Healthy
Care:
Provide suitable sunlight, well-drained soil, and consistent moisture without waterlogging.
Prevention:
Maintain good airflow, keep the growing area clean, and monitor leaves and fruit regularly for signs of disease or stress.
General Guidance:
Avoid both prolonged drought and excessive watering. Adjust care according to local growing conditions.

﻿Plant: Cherry
Condition: Healthy
Care:
Provide adequate sunlight and well-drained soil. Maintain appropriate soil moisture without prolonged waterlogging.
Prevention:
Maintain good airflow, remove diseased or fallen plant material where practical, and regularly inspect leaves, flowers, and fruit.
General Guidance:
Healthy plants should be monitored regularly so early signs of disease or environmental stress can be identified.

﻿Plant: Corn
Condition: Healthy
Care:
Provide adequate sunlight, suitable soil moisture, and balanced nutrients appropriate for the crop growth stage.
Prevention:
Monitor leaves regularly, maintain appropriate plant spacing, manage crop residues, and use healthy planting material.
General Guidance:
Avoid both prolonged drought and waterlogging. Regular monitoring helps identify disease or nutrient problems early.

﻿Plant: Grape
Condition: Healthy
Care:
Provide adequate sunlight, well-drained soil, suitable irrigation, and good canopy airflow.
Prevention:
Monitor leaves, shoots, and fruit regularly. Maintain sanitation and remove diseased or fallen plant material where practical.
General Guidance:
Avoid prolonged leaf wetness and maintain balanced plant nutrition appropriate for the growing stage.

﻿Plant: Peach
Condition: Healthy
Care:
Provide adequate sunlight, well-drained soil, and consistent moisture without waterlogging.
Prevention:
Monitor leaves, shoots, and fruit regularly. Maintain good airflow and remove diseased or fallen plant material where practical.
General Guidance:
Balanced nutrition, appropriate irrigation, and regular monitoring support healthy growth.

﻿Plant: Pepper Bell
Condition: Healthy
Care:
Provide adequate sunlight, well-drained fertile soil, and consistent moisture without waterlogging.
Prevention:
Maintain good airflow, monitor leaves and fruit regularly, keep tools clean, and avoid unnecessary prolonged leaf wetness.
General Guidance:
Provide balanced nutrition appropriate for the growth stage and monitor the plant regularly for early signs of stress or disease.

﻿Plant: Potato
Condition: Healthy
Care:
Keep soil consistently moist, especially during tuber development, but avoid waterlogging. Provide full sun and loose, well-drained soil.
Prevention:
Practice crop rotation, maintain good airflow, use healthy planting material, and monitor leaves regularly.
General Guidance:
Avoid prolonged leaf wetness and maintain balanced nutrition appropriate for crop growth.

﻿Plant: Raspberry
Condition: Healthy
Care:
Provide adequate sunlight, well-drained soil, and consistent moisture without waterlogging.
Prevention:
Maintain good airflow, keep the growing area clean, and monitor leaves, flowers, and fruit regularly.
General Guidance:
Use appropriate support and pruning practices where needed and maintain balanced nutrition.

﻿Plant: Soybean
Condition: Healthy
Care:
Provide adequate sunlight, suitable soil moisture, and well-drained soil. Maintain nutrition appropriate for the crop growth stage.
Prevention:
Use healthy seed, monitor plants regularly, maintain suitable field conditions, and manage weeds appropriately.
General Guidance:
Avoid prolonged waterlogging and monitor leaves and stems for early signs of disease or nutrient stress.

﻿Plant: Strawberry
Condition: Healthy
Care:
Provide adequate sunlight, well-drained soil, and consistent moisture without waterlogging.
Prevention:
Maintain clean growing areas, good airflow, appropriate spacing, and monitor leaves and fruit regularly.
General Guidance:
Water near the soil rather than unnecessarily wetting foliage and remove damaged or diseased plant material where practical.

﻿Plant: Tomato
Condition: Healthy
Care: Provide adequate sunlight, consistent soil moisture without waterlogging, good drainage, and sufficient airflow. Water near the soil surface when possible.
Prevention: Monitor leaves and stems regularly, remove dead plant material, keep tools clean, and maintain appropriate spacing.
General Guidance: Healthy tomato plants should be monitored regularly so that changes in leaf color, shape, spots, or growth can be detected early.

Plant: Potato
Watering: Keep soil consistently moist, especially during tuber development, but avoid waterlogging.
Sunlight: Full sun is preferred.
Soil: Loose, well-drained soil.
Common problems: Early blight and late blight.
Care: Rotate crops, maintain airflow, remove heavily infected foliage, and avoid prolonged leaf wetness.

Plant: Tomato
Watering: Keep soil evenly moist but not waterlogged. Check the top layer before watering.
Sunlight: Usually prefers about 6-8 hours of direct sunlight.
Soil: Well-drained fertile soil.
Common problems: Early blight, late blight, leaf mold, nutrient deficiency.
Care: Improve airflow, avoid wetting leaves unnecessarily, remove severely infected leaves, and keep tools clean.
